ai.badge_label: Made by AI: what does that mean?
ai.check: So check the subject and description before you use them. 'Edit text' lets you correct them; they only go to Commons when you upload the Commons draft.
ai.check_completion: Compare it with the cut-out. Use it at most as an illustration, clearly marked as completed by AI; never as a source or as a cut-out on Commons.
ai.check_detection: So check the cut-out (PNG and JPG) before you save it or take it to Commons. If the shape is not right, choose JPG (the rectangle) in the Commons draft.
ai.check_kind: The certainty is the model's own estimate, not a measured score. Check the kind yourself; it does not go to Commons.
ai.check_page: The search terms are only suggestions for the AI image detection; you choose what it finds yourself. Check the summary before you use it for anything.
ai.edited: This text was changed by hand after the AI answer.
ai.risk: A language model can be wrong: it can misread what it sees, be too certain, or make up names, dates and places that are nowhere in the image.
ai.risk_completion: What is in the holes is invented: the model does not know what was behind the other thing in the original. The rest of the image may have changed a little too, as the model draws the whole image anew, at a lower resolution.
ai.risk_detection: The detection can be wrong: the shape can hold a little too much or too little, it can be something other than the label says, or two things can be found together as one object.
ai.score_detection: For this object the score is {score}% (0% is doubt, 100% is certain).
ai.title: Made by AI
ai.what: This subject and description were written by a language model ({model}, Meta's AI image description). The model was shown the cut-out, with details of the file on Commons as context: title, description, categories and the caption of the cut-out.
ai.what_completion: This version was made by an image model ({model}, Meta's Muse Image). It got the cut-out on white, asked to fill in only the white holes in the same style, without looking anything up on the internet.
ai.what_detection: This object was found by the AI image detection ({model}, Meta's Segment Anything). The model looked for what you asked (a search term, a click or a rectangle) and returned a box and the shape of the object, with a score for how sure it is.
ai.what_kind: The kind and the certainty were chosen by a language model ({model}, Meta's AI image description): the kind from a fixed list (such as drawing, photograph, coat of arms, map), the certainty from high, medium or low.
ai.what_page: This summary and these search terms were made by a language model ({model}, Meta's AI page overview), which looked at the whole image, with details of the file on Commons as context.
bulk.dedupe_help: Objects that show the same thing (nearly the same frame) become one; the others are kept in it under 'also'. All = all visible objects. Free. Unlike grouping, where different objects together become one.
bulk.describe_help: All = all visible objects without a description; per kind = only those of one search term. Paid, with the amount next to it; you confirm first.
bulk.describe_kind_help: Have the visible objects of this kind without a description described (paid; you confirm first).
bulk.title: Bulk actions
bulk.trash_all_title: All visible objects to the trash?
bulkdescribe.editing_all: You are changing the settings for all {n} objects.
bulkdescribe.editing_one: You are changing the settings for '{name}' only.
bulkdescribe.hint_help: For instance to focus on one thing. Goes along with every object; it does not become the caption and does not go to Commons.
bulkdescribe.margin_help: How much space around each cut-out the AI sees (see the preview beside it). Here it is 0%: the AI only sees the object itself, so other things in the image do not colour the description. More space gives context, such as text around an image.
bulkdescribe.model_sees: what the AI sees of '{name}' (red: the cut-out)
bulkdescribe.prompt_for: as it goes to the model, for '{name}'

bulkdescribe.reset_help: Puts the settings of every object back: Commons caption, 0% space, no hint.
bulkdescribe.settings_help: Click 'All objects' to change them for all, or one object to change only that one and see what the AI sees of it. The table shows what each object gets.
bulkdescribe.show_object: Show what the AI sees of '{name}'
bulkdescribe.title: Have objects described

bulkdescribe.unhappy_before: After describing, you change each description per object in the magnifier: click the eye

completion.filled_help: What the AI filled in: where the cut-out had no shape and the completed version is not white. Approximate, as the AI draws the whole image anew.
completion.help: Have the AI (Meta's Muse Image) fill in the white holes in the cut-out, for instance where something stood in front of the object in the original. The AI invents what is missing: the result is not a source and never goes to Commons as a cut-out.

completion.remove_confirm: Remove the AI-completed version? It does not go to the trash: the object forgets it, but the image is kept on the server for another {days} days. ‘Complete the image with AI’ then brings the same image back for free. After that it is cleaned up. The cut-out itself stays.

history.aside_help: Images you do not want in view for now. Drag one here or click the trash can; the arrow up, or dragging it back, returns it to Viewed. Nothing is lost.
history.clear: Clear the whole list (Viewed and Set aside)
history.clear_confirm:
Clear the whole Viewed list, including what is set aside? Only the list goes.

**What stays**
- The images stay on Commons.
- Your objects (what you found on the images, with their descriptions) are kept.
- Your saved cut-outs (the image files) are kept.

**Back to an image**
- Enter its name, URL or M-id in the input bar at the top and click Open,
- or click one of its objects on the {objects}.

**Really deleting**
To delete objects and cut-outs, use Move to trash on the object, then the {trash} on the {objects}.
history.remove_confirm:
Take '{name}' off the Viewed list altogether? Only the entry goes.

**What stays**
- The image stays on Commons.
- Your objects (what you found on the image, with their descriptions) are kept.
- Your saved cut-outs (the image files) are kept.

**Back to the image**
- Click {mid}: the image opens again and is back in Viewed. Later you can also enter {mid} in the input bar at the top and click Open,
- or click one of its objects on the {objects}.

**Really deleting**
To delete objects and cut-outs, use Move to trash on the object, then the {trash} on the {objects}.

layout.history_info_1: These are the images you opened in this browser, the latest on top, with a thumbnail. Click to open one again.
layout.history_info_2: If you no longer want an image in view, click the trash can or drag it to **Set aside** (at the bottom, with a header that folds). There the arrow up (or dragging it back) returns it to Viewed, and the red trash can takes it off the list altogether (after a confirmation). The image, your objects and cut-outs are always kept.
layout.history_info_3: Every column slides away with the arrow in its header to a narrow strip; a click on the strip opens it again. This is remembered in this browser, as is this list.
layout.history_intro: Images you opened in this browser.
layout.left_info_1: This lists every object found on this image: by the AI image detection, pointed at or drawn by you, or as a region that is already on Commons. Point at an object, in the list or in the image, and both light up.
layout.left_info_2: **Object or cut-out?** An object is what was found on the image: a frame (sometimes with its shape), a name, a status, and perhaps a description and a Commons concept. It is data only. A cut-out is the image file you make of an object with Save selection: a JPG of the frame and a PNG of the shape, in the full resolution of the original. Every cut-out belongs to an object; an object only has a cut-out once you save it.
layout.left_info_3: **Ticking** picks an object to keep; under Save and export, Save selection makes cut-outs of it. All, None and Invert pick in one go. Click a name to show the object in the image.
layout.left_info_4: **The pencil** (or double-clicking the name) gives an object a name of its own, like a layer in Photoshop. Enter saves, Esc cancels; clear the name and the object gets its automatic name back. The name is for the list, the magnifier and as the subject when completing with AI, not for Commons.
layout.left_info_5: **The eye** (or the thumbnail, or double-clicking in the image) opens the magnifier. There you have the AI describe the object (What is this?), edit the texts, choose 'depicts' items from Wikidata and put together the description for Commons.
layout.left_info_6: **The trash can** moves an object to the trash, with its cut-outs. You find it on the Objects page (at the top), tab Trash, and can restore it there. Only when you empty the trash are the object and its cut-outs really gone.
layout.left_info_7: **Bulk actions** (fold-out under the list), in four tabs: Describe has objects without a description described in one go (paid, with the amount on the button); Deduplicate merges duplicates; Group turns several objects into one; Trash throws them away. Each for the ticked objects or for all visible ones, grouping and trashing also per kind. Only Describe costs money.
layout.left_info_8: **Save and export** (fold-out below that): Save selection makes cut-outs of the ticked objects, in the full resolution of the original; Download (zip) gives you the cut-outs; To Commons gets them ready for upload (uploading only happens after you confirm). The retention periods are there too. A button is disabled when there is nothing to do. Everything you do is saved automatically.
layout.left_intro: The objects on this image. Look at them, have them described, tick what you want to keep and save it under Save and export.
layout.resize_history: Width of the Viewed column (drag, arrow keys; double-click resets)
layout.resize_left: Width of the left column (drag, arrow keys; double-click resets)
layout.resize_objects: Width of the objects column (drag, arrow keys; double-click resets)
layout.resize_right: Width of the right column (drag, arrow keys; double-click resets)
layout.right_info_1: In this column you have the whole image described and find objects on it. The objects go to the column on the right, where you look at them and keep them as cut-outs. From top to bottom:
layout.right_info_2: **From Commons** (only when there are any) comes first: regions and notes that are already on Commons, free. What people already put on Commons comes before new AI suggestions. **AI suggestions for this image**: the AI looks at the whole image, describes it (also as a Commons caption of at most 250 characters) and suggests search terms. Click a search term to have those objects found, or detect them all in one go.
layout.right_info_3: **Search**: type what you are looking for, for example 'coat of arms' or 'portrait'. **Point or draw**: click one object in the image, or drag a rectangle (drawing is free).
layout.right_info_4: **Crop in CropTool**: crop the original itself, with another tool. Describing and merging what you found is done in the column on the right.
layout.right_info_5: Buttons with an amount cost money; you always see the amount and confirm first. The (i) button with each section explains more.
layout.right_intro: Let the AI describe the image and find objects, or point at or draw them yourself. What is found goes to the right.
legend.dik: thicker: chosen in the list or under the mouse
legend.info_1: Every colour means one thing, so you can read the image at a glance.
legend.info_3: **Mask** (the coloured shape over an object, when the AI image detection found its outline): its **kind**. One colour per kind of object, i.e. per search term or, for a region from Commons, its name; a name you gave it yourself with the pencil decides the colour, and at the tick boxes the object then counts under both that name and its search term (all plates one colour, all wine glasses another); the dot before each object in the list has the same colour. With only one kind on the image, the masks take the colour of their box (red selected, blue not selected). A group of different kinds keeps the colour of its box, and is counted under each of its kinds at the tick boxes.
legend.info_4: **Outline of a mask**: always white with a thin dark edge. It has no meaning of its own: it only makes the shape readable on light and dark images.
legend.info_5: **Show only these masks**: every kind has a checkbox; ticked kinds are shown (all of them to start with). Untick a kind to hide its masks; those objects fade. Together with the checkboxes of the boxes: an object stays in full view when both its kind and its status are ticked. **All · None · Invert** work as in the object list. This only changes what you see; nothing is selected or removed. While you use the search box above the object list, what you typed is a tick box too, with the number of matches; while it is ticked, all of those objects show.
legend.info_6: **Masks**, **Boxes** and **Labels** above the image switch the masks, the boxes and the names on or off. Everything here is free.
legend.info_label: What the colours in the image mean
legend.kind_only: Untick to hide the masks of {kind} (the object fades)
legend.query_only: Everything that matches your search in the object list. Untick to fade it and hide its masks.
legend.status_only: Untick to fade the objects with this colour of box

objects.describe_help: Have the AI image description describe every selected object that has no description yet. Objects that already have one are skipped. Costs money per object; you confirm first.

objects.describe_note_all_done: All {selected} selected objects already have a description, so there is nothing to describe. To describe a single object again, open it with the eye, tab “What is this?”, and there use the “Describe this image again” button.

objects.open_augmented: Open the AI-augmented version in the magnifier
objects.rename_help: Rename: double-click the name or click the pencil. Enter saves, Esc cancels; empty goes back to the automatic name. Only for the list, not for Commons.
objects.resize_facets: Width of the filters: drag, or arrow keys (double-click: back)
objects.saved_expiry: The saved files are removed on {date} unless you use them before then (retention period). Downloading or saving again resets the clock; on Commons they are kept.
objects.search_help: Search the objects' name, search term, item, caption and description.
objects.search_info_1: Type one or more words: only objects that contain **every word** stay in the list and in the image. Capitals do not matter; part of a word is enough ('lem' finds 'lemon').
objects.search_info_3: **Dutch and English**: you can search in both languages. The search terms are English ('lemon'), the Dutch names are kept too ('citroen'), and the AI description is there in both languages; so 'lemon' and 'citroen' both find the lemons.
objects.search_info_4:
**What it does**: searching changes nothing about your objects, only what you see.
- Objects that do not match disappear for the moment from the list and from the image.
- All · None · Invert tick or untick only the objects found.
- 'All' in the bulk actions (for example Group all) also only concerns the objects found. Search 'lemon' and click Group all: only the lemons are grouped.
- Ticks on objects you do not see for the moment stay. Save selection still takes them along. (The Minimum certainty slider works differently: what it hides is also unticked.)
- Clear the box (the cross) to see everything again. Free.
objects.search_result: {n} of {total} objects match your search; All, None and Invert and 'all' in the bulk actions only concern these. Clear the search box to see everything again.
objects.shape_removed: SAM's shape is gone; '{name}' has its rectangle again.
objects.show_in_folder_help: Opens the file manager on this computer, with the saved cut-out selected (only when the app runs on your own computer)
objects.tick_all_help: Tick the boxes of all objects in this list

original.add_position_help: This changes someone else's existing statement: the place (P2677) is added to it. Off by default.
original.button: Add to the structured data of this image (on Commons)
original.button_help: The search terms and found objects above are candidates for 'depicts' (P180) in the structured data on Commons, as is the description for the caption. Nothing goes to Commons by itself: in the window this button opens, you review the proposals, choose the right Wikidata item and tick what you approve. Free; kept as a draft, not yet on Commons.
original.button_pages: Not for a file with more pages: the data belongs to the whole file, not to one page.
original.caption_ai_too_long: The AI proposal is {n} characters; a caption on Commons is at most {max}.
original.caption_ask: Have the AI make a Commons caption
original.caption_choice_zelf: Write it yourself (starts with both texts; counts once you change it)
original.caption_level_note: The AI proposal comes from the description of the image, which was not asked in the Commons caption setting and is therefore often too long. Have the AI make a Commons caption (paid; the current description goes to Earlier descriptions), or shorten the proposal below (free).
original.caption_no_ai: No AI proposal yet: have the image described under AI suggestions for this image (paid). Writing your own is always possible.
original.caption_other_languages: Captions in other languages (stay as they are)
original.caption_replace_note: The old caption stays in the history of the page on Commons.
original.info_2: **With place**: every object on the image gets a statement of its own with its place (P2677, 'relative position within image'): the object's frame, in percentages of the whole image. Commons then shows where the item is, and this app reads it back next time as a region. Three lemons become three statements 'depicts: lemon', each with its own place.
original.info_3: **Without place** (box unticked): one statement 'depicts' without a place, even with more objects. Useful for something about the whole image, such as a genre or the maker.
original.info_4: **The pencil** chooses another Wikidata item, when the AI search term found the wrong one. **The red bin** removes a row you do not want to see; Show again brings it back. **All · None · Invert** set the ticks of all proposals.
original.info_5: Nothing goes twice onto the original: what is already there or already goes with the upload of a cut-out is not added again, and a statement with a place comes before one without.
original.intro: Add to the structured data of the whole image: what the app found, next to what is already on Commons. The app only adds; you change an existing statement or caption on Commons itself.
original.no_objects: no object on the image yet
original.proposals_none: No proposals yet. Have the image described, find objects, or add an item yourself below.
original.resolving: Looking up the search terms on Wikidata (free)…
original.rules: Nothing goes twice onto the original: what is already there or already goes with a cut-out is not added again, and a statement with a place comes before one without.
original.saved: Draft saved. It is ready for later; nothing changed on Commons.
original.source_gekozen: chosen by you for a cut-out
original.terms_without_objects: Search terms without a found object ({n})
original.title: Structured data of this image
original.to_commons_later: Saving on Commons comes later (phase 2, after logging in), first on a test wiki. Until then you save a draft.
original.too_long: A caption is longer than 250 characters; make it shorter to save.
original.too_long_in: A caption is longer than 250 characters ({languages}); make it shorter in the Captions tab, or untick Add, to save.
original.with_position_default: It is on by default: with a place the data is most useful, also for others.
original.with_position_help: With place: one statement per object, with its place on the image (P2677). Without: one statement.
original.with_position_off: **Without place (unticked)**: one statement 'depicts: {item}' without a frame. It only says that it is somewhere on the image. Choose this for something about the whole image, such as a genre ('still life') or the maker.
original.with_position_on: **With place (ticked)**: on Commons, 'depicts: {item}' also says where it is on the image: the object's frame, as 'relative position within image' (P2677). Here that is {n} object(s), so {n} statement(s), each with its own frame. Commons and this app then show a rectangle per object.
original.with_upload: {n} of these get their place on the original already with the upload of their cut-out ({names}); that becomes one statement per object, not two.

panel.bulk_trash_help: Move all objects of one kind to the trash in one go, after a confirmation. Only the visible ones (above the minimum certainty). You can undo it straight away, or later on the Objects page, tab Trash.

panel.commons_depicts_click: Click an item to have the AI image detection look for it; what is found gets that item as 'depicts' straight away.
panel.commons_depicts_intro_after: in the image, but without a specific location / bounding box.

panel.commons_edit_link: Show the depicts statements on Commons
panel.commons_read_again_help: The app keeps what it reads from Commons for a day. If you just added something on Commons, such as a caption or 'depicts', read the file again. Free.
panel.croptool_help: Want to crop or straighten the whole image? Use CropTool, the usual tool on Commons. It opens this file; there you choose the crop yourself.
panel.description_help: The AI describes the whole image at the chosen length: what kind of image it is, what is shown and the text that can be read on it, in Dutch and English. Use the pencil to edit the text yourself; earlier versions are below. The Commons caption setting gives a text of at most 250 characters, suitable as a caption on Commons.
panel.draw_help: Drag over the image to choose a cut-out by hand; it becomes an object of its own that you can save and take to Commons like the others. Without this mode, Shift-drag does the same.
panel.from_commons_help: The regions already on Commons under 'depicts' (the yellow rectangles) and the file notes. Free; every region becomes an object of its own.
panel.from_commons_intro: What people have already recorded about this image on Commons. Reading it is free. The app only adds; you change an existing caption or 'depicts' on Commons itself.
panel.group_all_help: Make one object of all objects of this search term, with one frame and their masks together. Free; Ungroup puts them back.
panel.info_commons_2: **Captions**: the short descriptions of the image on Commons, in every language there is. Read only. They go along as context when you have the AI describe the image.
panel.info_commons_3: **'Depicts' with a region**: items with a place on the image. The Regions from Commons button turns each region into an object of its own, which you can describe, save and cut out. Free: no AI is involved.
panel.info_commons_4: **'Depicts' without a region**: items without a place on the image, as buttons. Click an item to have the AI image detection look for it (paid); what is found gets that item as 'depicts' straight away. Use the pencil to change the search word. These items also go along as context for the AI.
panel.info_commons_5: **File notes**: rectangles with text that someone put on the file page with ImageAnnotator. With Regions from Commons they also become objects, with their text as caption. Free.
panel.info_commons_6: The app changes nothing of this on Commons. To change or remove an existing caption, 'depicts' or note, do so on Commons itself.
panel.info_croptool_1: CropTool (croptool2.toolforge.org) crops, straightens or rotates a file on Commons and saves the result as a new version or a new file. You log in there with your Commons account.
panel.info_croptool_2: The Commons Mineventory does something else: it turns objects in the image into separate new files, and never overwrites the original. CropTool is for cropping the original itself. CropTool does not take over a box from the Commons Mineventory.
panel.info_croptool_3: Only for single-page images; not for PDF, DjVu or multi-page TIFF.
panel.info_point_1: Point: switch it on and click an object in the image. The AI image detection (SAM) then finds the shape of that one object. Each click is one paid call.
panel.info_point_2: Draw: switch it on and drag a rectangle over the image. It becomes an object right away, without AI and for free. You can also do this without the switch, with Shift-drag.
panel.info_search_1: Type what you are looking for, for example 'coat of arms' or 'portrait'. The AI image detection (SAM) finds every place in the image that matches, with a box and a mask.
panel.info_search_2: One concept per search works best. Combine with AND, exclude with NOT (what you exclude is shown as excluded). Dutch terms are first translated into English.
panel.info_search_3: Each search is one paid call; the same term on the same image then comes from the cache.
panel.info_suggestions_1: The AI image description (Muse Spark) first looks at the whole image. You get a short summary and a list of search terms for what it shows, each with the expected number.
panel.info_suggestions_2: Click a search term to see where it is on the image: the AI image detection (SAM) finds those places and makes objects of them. Locate all objects, right behind the search terms, searches all ticked terms in one go; untick a term that should not go along (your choice is remembered in this browser). The number on a search term is how many objects from it are on the image now.
panel.info_suggestions_3: The overview is kept. The description and the search terms can each be made anew (a new, paid question for that part only) or removed (free). With both removed, you can ask 'What is on this page?' again; the first answer then comes from the cache for free.

retention.cache: Found objects (the data: frame, name, description) and AI descriptions: **{n} days**. A page not opened for that long goes, with all its objects and descriptions. Asking again then costs money again.
retention.cutouts: Saved cut-outs and masks (the image files, JPG and PNG): **{n} days**. After that the files are deleted; the object stays and you can save it again. If you want to keep a cut-out, download it (on its own or as a zip) or bring it to Commons.
retention.intro: The Commons Mineventory is **not an archive**: not everything is kept forever. Each period counts from the last use, so opening or downloading again resets the clock.
retention.keep: Cut-outs that are on Commons are kept there for good. The overview of costs (the usage log) **is always kept**.
retention.originals: The original file from Commons and other data from Commons: **{n} days**. They are always on Commons and are fetched again for free.
retention.short: Saved cut-outs are removed after {n} days without use; download them as a zip or bring them to Commons if you want to keep them.
retention.title: How long is this kept?
rights.upload_blocked: The original is under discussion; uploading cut-outs is switched off.
rights_help.alleen_vs: Free in the United States only ({{PD-US-only}}). That is not actually allowed on Commons.
rights_help.in_orde: Public domain or a free licence, without trademark, personality rights, deletion request or pending licence review. Cut-outs may be uploaded.
rights_help.merk: The original is marked as a trademark, or the cut-out looks like a logo or advertisement. Upload only with a reason.
rights_help.naamsvermelding: The licence requires attribution (e.g. CC BY). The author and licence of the original are always added to the new page.
rights_help.persoonlijkheidsrechten: The original has {{Personality rights}} and the cut-out shows a person. Mind how the image is used.
rights_help.ter_discussie: The original has a deletion request, a copyright notice or a licence review that is not yet confirmed. Uploading is switched off.
rights_reason.alleen_vs: Free in the United States only ({{PD-US-only}}); that is not allowed on Commons.
rights_reason.controle_open: The licence review is not yet confirmed: {detail}.
rights_reason.naamsvermelding: Attribution required ({detail}): author and licence go into the new page.
rights_reason.persoonlijkheidsrechten: The original has personality rights ({{Personality rights}}).
sdc.fact_help: This follows from the cut-out file itself (type, checksum, size, dimensions) and so cannot be edited.
terms.objects_cutouts: **Object or cut-out?** An object is what was found on the image: a frame (sometimes with its shape), a name, a status, and perhaps a description and a Commons concept. It is data only. A cut-out is the image file you make of an object with Save selection: a JPG of the frame and a PNG of the shape, in the full resolution of the original. Every cut-out belongs to an object; an object only has a cut-out once you save it.
upload.confirm: I have checked the description, the licence and the rights. The files will be uploaded in my name.
upload.disabled: Uploading is still off (phase 2). Copy the wikitext or download the zip.
upload.intro: All saved cut-outs of this file, with their draft. Checked by default: only 'No rights concerns' and 'Attribution required'.
upload.no_file: Choose a file on the start page first.
upload.nothing_saved: No saved cut-outs yet. Select objects and choose 'Save selection'.

usage.capped: Only the latest {n} calls are listed and searched here; the totals above count everything.
usage.intro: Paid calls to AI image detection (SAM 3.1) and AI image description (Muse Spark), with estimated costs. In test mode everything is free and this stays empty.
usage.model_muse_image: fills the gaps in a cut-out
usage.models_info_1: All four are models from Meta, used through the Meta Model API. Every paid call is logged here with its estimated cost.
usage.models_info_2: **sam-3.1** (SAM 3.1), the AI image detection: finds objects from a search word, a click or a drawn box, and draws their outline (mask). US$ 0.0025 per call.
usage.models_info_3: **muse-spark-1.3** (Muse Spark, standard), the AI image description: answers 'What is this?' and 'What is on this page?'. Used when an image is not certainly in the public domain or has a rights label. US$ 1.25 per million tokens in, US$ 4.25 out.
usage.models_info_4: **muse-spark-1.3-contributor** (Muse Spark, Contributor): the same work, much cheaper. Only for images in the public domain without rights labels, because Meta may use that input to train its models. US$ 0.10 per million tokens in, US$ 0.20 out.
usage.models_info_5: **muse-image-1.0** (Muse Image): makes the AI-augmented version of a cut-out by filling in what is missing. It invents those parts, so the result is not a source. US$ 0.01 per image.
usage.models_info_title: The AI models in this log
